quizzes.stem: A product owner asks that a new feature for writing customer emails must "sound professional". The team wants a requirement that a test can fail. Which version is best?

options.a: Ninety percent of outputs in a fixed sample of forty tickets pass a tone rubric that a grader applies
options.b: The support lead reads a handful of outputs before release and judges that they sound professional
options.c: The prompt gives the instruction to write in a professional and courteous voice whenever it replies
options.d: Customers rate each email after sending, and the feature stays while the ratings stay positive

explanation.a: It states a rate over a fixed sample and names a grader, which is what the page asks of a quality requirement: a number over that set.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a requirement that only a person's impression can settle is a wish", and a read-through by one lead is only an impression.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a rule in a prompt "is only a request to the model", and a prompt line is not a test.
explanation.d: Ruled out because ratings after sending are an operational signal, while the acceptance criterion must be "written before the first prompt is tried".

quizzes.stem: A draft spec for an invoice-extraction feature lists the fields to extract, the accepted file types and the expected accuracy. Which missing item should a reviewer ask the team to add first?

options.a: The exact system prompt that the developers plan to use for the extraction
options.b: One expected output string for each sample invoice, compared character by character
options.c: What the screen shows the user when a call to the model errors, is refused or stops early
options.d: A recorded demo of the extraction running cleanly on a handful of sample invoices

explanation.c: Failure behaviour is the row the page says teams forget, because a spec without it produces code without it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the quality number is "written before the first prompt is tried", so the prompt is an implementation choice that comes after the spec.
explanation.b: Ruled out because quality "is stated as a rate over a set of examples, not as a single expected string".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a demo can be one that "impresses everyone and cannot say whether it is done", so it adds no line a test can fail.

quizzes.stem: A feature must label two million archived tickets overnight, and nobody reads the labels until morning. The team proposes a pool of workers that call the API one ticket at a time all night. Which change fits the requirement best?

options.a: Stream every reply from the workers so that the first words of each label arrive sooner
options.b: Hand the whole job to the batch interface, which halves the price and runs unattended
options.c: Move the workers to the fastest tier so that the overnight window is certain to be enough
options.d: Chain a second call after each label that checks the label before the result is stored

explanation.b: Nobody is waiting and volume is large, which the page assigns to a batch: "most batches finishing in less than 1 hour while reducing costs by 50%".
explanation.a: Ruled out because streaming "does not shorten the total time", and no reader is watching the words arrive.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a faster tier is correct only "if your evaluation set (page 1) says its quality holds", and it does not change the cost.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "chaining calls multiplies latency" and also cost, and the requirement gives no reason for a second call.

quizzes.stem: A requirement says customer data may only be processed in the United States. A developer plans to use `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` and set `inference_geo` to `"us"` on every request. What does the page predict?

options.a: The calls succeed and are billed at 1.1 times the standard rate for inference kept in the US
options.b: The calls succeed and run in any region, because the unsupported setting is quietly dropped
options.c: The calls fail with a 429 error, because the capacity inside the US for that model is limited
options.d: The calls fail with a 400 error, because the setting is not supported on that model

explanation.d: The page says a request that sets the geography on Claude Haiku 4.5 or an earlier model "return a 400 error".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the 1.1 times price belongs to models where the setting is "supported on Claude 4.6 and later", which excludes this one.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the documentation says such requests "return a 400 error", so the setting is rejected and not dropped.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Rate limits are shared across all geos", so the setting opens no separate US pool whose capacity could run out.

quizzes.stem: A team's nightly report job started returning slightly different summaries after a provider released an update. The code names its model with an alias. What is the underlying mistake?

options.a: The evaluation set was too small to notice that the summaries had started to drift
options.b: The id was never pinned, so the new version went live with no regression run
options.c: The summaries were never written down as requirements before the first prompt was tried
options.d: The job logged no request ids, so nobody could trace which call had changed

explanation.b: An alias that moves "changes behaviour under you", and the routine is to pin an id and change it on purpose, with a regression run.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the routine asks for "a regression run of the evaluation set on every change", and no set was run on this change at all, whatever its size.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a missing spec is a separate fault, while the symptom is described by "a silent change of model is a silent change of behaviour".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the request id is logged to "include it when you contact support about a specific request", which helps a trace but does not stop the change.

quizzes.stem: A client library crashes whenever the API adds a new field to a response, although the API's documented rules allow additions. What is the best fix?

options.a: Pin an older API version header to stop any new property from appearing in the reply body
options.b: Validate each reply against a strict schema and reject any reply that has extra fields
options.c: Wrap the parsing step in a retry with backoff so that a later reply parses cleanly
options.d: Take only the properties the code needs and skip everything else in the reply

explanation.d: The page says to be tolerant of additions and strict about what you send, which means reading only what the code uses.
explanation.a: Ruled out because earlier versions are deprecated and "may be unavailable for new users", and additions arrive within the current one.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a retry cannot help, because the same reply is parsed the same way again".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a client that rejects an unknown field or an unknown event type breaks on a change that is allowed".

quizzes.stem: A feature must return a complete answer to a waiting user within two seconds. The team's design is a chain of five calls, each taking about one second. Which action fits best?

options.a: Stream the final stage so that its first words appear sooner for the person waiting
options.b: Merge or drop stages until the summed time of what remains sits inside the budget
options.c: Request a higher usage plan from the provider so that each individual call runs faster
options.d: Move the whole pipeline to asynchronous batches, which are processed at half the price

explanation.b: Chained calls add up, so the fix is to cut the sequence: "a requirement of two seconds rules out a five-call pipeline".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "streaming does not shorten the total time", and the requirement is for the complete answer.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a higher tier "does not make one call finish sooner".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a batch "is the right design when nobody is waiting", and a user is waiting.

quizzes.stem: After a team swaps its model for a newer id, the support lead says the new one feels better. What should happen before release?

options.a: Rerun the fixed evaluation set on the candidate id and compare it with the acceptance rate
options.b: Accept the lead's impression, since the replacement is the more recent release of the family
options.c: Switch to the moving alias so that every later upgrade arrives without any change in the code
options.d: Compare the monthly bill of the two models over a single representative week of production traffic

explanation.a: The maintain routine is to re-run the evaluation set against the new model and compare, so the change is judged on numbers.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a requirement that only a person's impression can settle is a wish".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a silent change of model is a silent change of behaviour".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a bill covers cost alone, while the routine says to "re-run the evaluation set against the new model" for quality.

quizzes.stem: A feature runs comfortably under its entry-level request limit on average, but a quarterly campaign sends four times that rate for ten minutes, and the first requests of the burst are refused. Which response fits best?

options.a: Spread the traffic over a longer window so the peak load stays under the allowance
options.b: Keep the current tier, since the daily average stays well below the request limit
options.c: Shorten every reply from the model so that each single request counts for less against the limit
options.d: Switch the residency setting to global so that a second and separate pool becomes available

explanation.a: The bucket can be emptied by a burst whatever the average is, so the plan must fit the peak, and smoothing the load over time is one of the page's answers.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "write the peak, not the mean".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a request counts against the request limit however short its reply is".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "rate limits are shared across all geos", so no second pool appears.

quizzes.stem: A help site must answer visitors only from the company's own policy documents, one answer for each visitor, with the visitor waiting. Which design fits best?

options.a: Chain three separate calls that draft, check and polish the reply before it is shown
options.b: Run an agent loop that explores the documents until the loop is satisfied with what it found
options.c: Retrieve the passages that match each question and send them with it in a single call
options.d: Send each question in one streamed call and let the model answer from what it knows

explanation.c: Answers that must come from the company's own documents point to retrieval followed by one call.
explanation.b: Ruled out because an agent loop is for when "the path depends on what is found and cannot be listed in advance".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a chain is for "several dependent steps, each checkable", and three calls would also cost latency.
explanation.d: Ruled out because one call alone fits "one answer from the input alone", and for the company's documents "the model's training does not contain them".
